question: Why did the principal mass-loss region of the kerogen begin about 50 C later under air than under nitrogen?
question_long: Why did the principal mass-loss region of oil shale kerogen begin about 50 C later under air than under nitrogen?
expect: premise false: it began about 50 C EARLIER under air (abstract; sec. 3.1)
rendered: The principal mass-loss region of the kerogen began about 50 °C earlier under air than under nitrogen, not later. This is evident from Figure 4a, which shows the TG curves of oil shale under air and nitrogen atmospheres at different heating rates.
